name: Agente
summary: Agente brings concrete learning-platform and commerce experience. Its portfolio identifies UX/UI work for Automation Academy, and its Atterley case describes information architecture, catalog and product pages, and a checkout redesign.
limits_and_questions: Some of this work is historical, so confirm who would staff your project today and the exact scope proposed. A PropTech service-page claim alone is not evidence of real-estate product work.

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: Arounda
summary: Arounda is a fintech-focused studio. Its PIIFUND case describes banking, microloan and insurance flows, including onboarding and use on weak connections, with UX, wireframe and UI work rather than a logo-only relationship.
limits_and_questions: Deployment and compliance details are agency-reported. Ask for current, comparable financial-product work; this case does not demonstrate expertise in unrelated niches.

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: Aufait UX
summary: Aufait UX documents work in three distinct areas: broker-facing property search and booking for DAMAC, field research and distribution workflows for iD Fresh, and information architecture for Parul University's large website.
limits_and_questions: The Parul project is an institutional website, not a learning-management system. DAMAC covers an agent/broker workflow, not every tenant or property-transaction use case, so ask for examples closer to your users if they differ.
project_evidence: DAMAC Agents; iD Fresh; Parul University

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: Cieden
summary: Cieden is relevant for complex clinical and practice-management software. Its Clinicmaster account describes modernization across patient records, billing and charting, with workflow and design-system considerations.
limits_and_questions: The source describes a validated direction ready for continued rollout, not an independently audited platform-wide deployment or compliance certification. The Sitenna case alone is not logistics or real-estate evidence; ask for a comparable project if that is your sector.

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: CorLab Tech
summary: CorLab Tech is a development-oriented firm whose public service pages describe operational dashboards, maps, and transport, warehouse and delivery software. Its list position reflects editorial judgment, not a measured comparison of client outcomes.
limits_and_questions: Public evidence comes from CorLab Tech's service pages; there is no named logistics client case, usability testing or verified result. Ask for a comparable named logistics project, the UX research/design team who would work on yours, and what they actually shipped. Service claims in healthcare or AI are likewise unverified.
project_evidence: Data visualization and logistics service pages

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: Fantasy
summary: Fantasy brings enterprise AI and bank-employee workflow experience. It describes vision and interface work and a coded design-system contribution for BNY Eliza, an internal financial-services AI tool rather than a marketing website.
limits_and_questions: Fantasy's documented role covers the vision and design-system scope; the overall platform, model, bank adoption and reported operational results belong to the wider program. Ask which parts of the product its team designed and built.

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: Fuselab Creative
summary: Fuselab Creative works on data-rich clinical and administrative products, conversational data tools and robotics interfaces. Its sources cover distinct contexts, including warehouse fleet and mission controls relevant to logistics.
limits_and_questions: Provider-facing tools, public-health reporting, industrial robotics and warehouse operations are separate projects, and design work is distinct from hardware engineering. Deployment, safety and clinical outcomes are not independently verified, so ask for references from the context closest to yours.
project_evidence: ClyHealth; DHCS; Stardog Voicebox; Robodog AGV; Hyperfab

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: Fuzzy Math
summary: Fuzzy Math brings enterprise healthcare research and reusable interaction-pattern experience. The source describes work across clinical, imaging and administrative products, including data interpretation and legacy-system consistency.
limits_and_questions: The account covers R&D and product exploration, so not every illustrated concept shipped, and it is not evidence of medical-device certification. Ask which concepts reached production.

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: GoInvo
summary: GoInvo is a strong option for healthcare systems and research-centered AI. Maya provides concrete home-health workflow evidence, and Facto describes guided AI research, contextual tools and source transparency.
limits_and_questions: Maya's working-product status is agency-reported. Facto combines shipped improvements with prototypes for future work, and usage figures are unaudited; ask which features are live.

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: Guidea
summary: Guidea is a healthcare-focused specialist. Its public portfolio names platform-design and population-health contexts, offering industry depth beyond general product studios.
limits_and_questions: The source is a portfolio overview with uneven project detail. Ask for a detailed project walkthrough or reference to confirm process and outcomes; partner product clearances are not agency-wide certification.
project_evidence: Amalgam Rx; Humana population-health platform; Express Scripts

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: HTEC Momentum
summary: HTEC Momentum (formerly Momentum Design Lab) brings supply-chain and ML-recommendation experience through Sifted, including reorganizing how shippers find actionable insight, and product-strategy and mobile trading-app design through Bitstamp.
limits_and_questions: HTEC's company-wide services and headcount describe the wider firm, not the design team you would get; confirm who would be assigned. Published results are agency-reported, not independently audited.

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: Lazarev.agency
summary: Lazarev.agency supports AI-assisted financial research through Rhea. Named cases also cover B2B chemical purchasing (Matta), property and co-ownership acquisition UX (CoHome), and wellness discovery, scheduling and personalization (WellSet).
limits_and_questions: WellSet is wellness work, not clinical/EHR expertise, and Matta is industrial commerce. CoHome covers property exploration and its website/funnel scope. Funding, acquisition, clinical outcomes and regulatory validation are not established by these cases.

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: Metalab
summary: Metalab shows real AI product examples, with selected portfolio items identifying product design and implementation contributions. A robotics-testing infrastructure entry also supports a limited simulation and developer-tools placement.
limits_and_questions: Its robotics evidence is portfolio-level simulation and testing work, not physical robot control. The portfolio mixes product, branding and website work, so ask for detail on the specific projects relevant to you.
project_evidence: Midjourney; Suno; robotics virtual-testing portfolio item

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: Netguru
summary: Netguru's Otodom case describes embedded property-marketplace research, design and testing; Chorus shows academic app-creation UX; and Aspit identifies healthcare product design and engineering for medical-professional software.
limits_and_questions: Netguru works in a combined design/engineering model, so confirm the design contribution on each project. Academic tooling is not general LMS experience, and Aspit's public process description is less detailed than leading specialist healthcare cases.

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: Neuron
summary: Neuron is relevant for health-insurance administration and medical-coding tools. Its case identifies workflow research with subject-matter experts, interface modernization and a React front-end contribution.
limits_and_questions: Insurance risk adjustment and medical coding are distinct from treatment decisions or bedside clinical software. Neuron is best suited to that operational context; ask for clinical examples if you need them.

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: Qubstudio
summary: Qubstudio has distinct named evidence across several niches: LinkIt! for student, parent and staff products; BluePallet for industrial commerce; and MyTower for transportation-management IA/UX. Its client portfolio also identifies banking work.
limits_and_questions: Ask for the project most relevant to your sector. MyTower and banking entries have less public depth than full case studies, its recruitment AI work is historical, and infrastructure branding work is not PropTech product evidence.
project_evidence: Ademrius; Gulf Bank/ila Bank; BluePallet; MyTower; LinkIt!; Wade & Wendy

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: Think Company
summary: Think Company brings healthcare research and family-provider experience. The source describes interviews, a telemedicine pilot and later product evolution with the care organization.
limits_and_questions: Healthcare outcomes belong to the wider health-system product, so ask which parts Think Company itself contributed. Its workforce-analytics work falls outside the categories covered here.

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: ustwo
summary: ustwo has the broadest documented coverage here, with separate cases rather than one generic claim: Fresenius for clinician and patient experiences, Brilliant for learning engagement, Pi for AI interaction and SharkClean for consumer robot controls. Other cases cover payments, fleet-driver tools and mobile commerce.
limits_and_questions: Breadth is not a quality score. EPI includes vision/prototype foundations, Brilliant includes a tested North Star concept, and Lush is historical. Alphabet here is BMW Group's mobility business, not Google's parent, and its driver app is not freight dispatch; consumer robotics is distinct from industrial fleet control.
project_evidence: Fresenius; Brilliant.org; Inflection Pi; Alphabet; SharkClean; EPI; Lush

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: UXDA
summary: UXDA is an explicit financial-UX specialist. Its UAB case describes redesigning customer banking tasks and mobile flows rather than a general corporate brand website.
limits_and_questions: UXDA's documented strength is financial services; its reputation does not imply expertise in unrelated sectors. Confirm the current team and relevant retail or corporate banking scope; published metrics are agency-reported.

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: UX Studio
summary: UX Studio offers a research-led AI-monitoring example and a distinct educational robotics example. Revolution describes configuration, coding and control, with research and testing involving children.
limits_and_questions: OverseeAI is proof-of-concept/MVP-stage work. Revolution supports both its Education and Robotics placements from a single case and does not establish industrial control expertise or broad LMS experience.

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.

name: Work & Co
summary: Work & Co has strong commerce credentials: its IKEA case covers the shopping app, website ecosystem and reusable design work. Its current client portfolio also lists a home-buying experience contribution for Lennar.
limits_and_questions: The real-estate placement is portfolio-level: the Lennar entry is much thinner than the IKEA case. Ask for a fuller account of the Lennar work before relying on it for a real-estate brief.

commercial_facts.note: Budgets, rates, offices and availability have not been researched.
